title: Third Word Worships Spiritual Lightness And Beliefs Security

questions.question: In the story, what do the two travelers stand for?
questions.answer: One stands for people who obey Allah’s law, and the other stands for people who follow their own wants.

questions.question: What does the road stand for?
questions.answer: It stands for a person’s life journey.

questions.question: Where does this life journey go?
questions.answer: It comes from the world of spirits, passes through the grave, and goes on to the Hereafter.

questions.question: In the comparison, what do the bag and the weapon stand for?
questions.answer: They stand for worship and fearing Allah.

questions.question: Even if worship feels heavy at first, what does the passage say is true about it?
questions.answer: It really brings ease and lightness.

questions.question: What important truth does a person say in prayer?
questions.answer: He says that only Allah is worthy of worship.

questions.question: When a believer knows Allah is the only Creator and Provider, who does he turn to for help?
questions.answer: He turns to Allah.

questions.question: Who controls harm and benefit?
questions.answer: Allah does.

questions.question: Why can the believer trust Allah’s choices?
questions.answer: Because Allah is Wise and Merciful.

questions.question: What does the believer do after understanding that all things are under Allah’s command?
questions.answer: He seeks safety with Allah and trusts Him.

questions.question: What does belief give a person during hard times?
questions.answer: It gives strong confidence and protection from fear.

questions.question: What good quality comes from belief and worship?
questions.answer: Courage.

questions.question: What bad quality comes from going the wrong way?
questions.answer: Cowardice.

questions.question: How would a person with a bright, believing heart react to a huge frightening event?
questions.answer: He would stay calm and see Allah’s power in it.

questions.question: How did the godless thinker react when he saw the comet?
questions.answer: He became very scared.

questions.question: Why does the passage say people need Allah so much?
questions.answer: Because people need many things, have little power, and face many troubles.

questions.question: What reaches farther than a person’s hand and strength?
questions.answer: His hopes, wishes, pain, and worries.

questions.question: For weak and needy people, what brings great good and happiness?
questions.answer: Worship, believing that Allah is One, trusting Allah, and submitting to Him.

questions.question: Which kind of person is shown by the traveler who follows Allah’s law?
questions.answer: A person who submits to Allah’s command.

questions.question: Which kind of person is shown by the other traveler?
questions.answer: A person who rebels and follows his own desires.

questions.question: What is the road of life like in this passage?
questions.answer: It is a path that moves from the spirit world to the grave and then to the Hereafter.

questions.question: What lesson do the bag and weapon teach?
questions.answer: Worship and fear of Allah may seem hard, but they help and protect a person.

questions.question: In prayer, what belief opens mercy for the worshipper?
questions.answer: Believing that only Allah is God.

questions.question: If Allah alone creates and provides, what does that teach the believer?
questions.answer: That he should depend on Allah, not on created things.

questions.question: Why does the worshipper make du‘a to Allah?
questions.answer: Because Allah’s mercy and kindness are great.

questions.question: If everything obeys Allah, how does that help the believer feel?
questions.answer: It helps him feel safe with Allah.

questions.question: What two things does the believer do with his heart when afraid?
questions.answer: He takes refuge in Allah and puts his trust in Him.

questions.question: What is the result of this trust?
questions.answer: He becomes stronger against troubles.

questions.question: According to the passage, where does real bravery come from?
questions.answer: From belief in Allah and worship.

questions.question: According to the passage, where does fearfulness come from?
questions.answer: From misguidance and sin.

questions.question: What example shows the strength of a believing heart?
questions.answer: Even something as huge as the earth blowing up would not shake his heart with fear.

questions.question: What example shows the weakness of a heart without faith?
questions.answer: A man without a sound heart became terrified by a comet.

questions.question: Does having only a clever mind make a person truly strong inside?
questions.answer: No. Without a sound heart, he can still be very afraid.

questions.question: Why is the human being described as weak?
questions.answer: Because he needs many things but has very little power and wealth.

questions.question: How far can a person’s needs and worries reach?
questions.answer: Very far, as far as his eyes and imagination can go.

questions.question: What is the main message at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Since people are weak and needy, worship and trusting Allah bring them great happiness and benefit.

questions.question: What are the two paths shown by the two travelers really about?
questions.answer: They are about obeying Allah or following selfish desires.

questions.question: What part of a person’s life does the road represent?
questions.answer: The whole journey of life until the Hereafter.

questions.question: What do worship and fear of Allah look like in the comparison?
questions.answer: They look like a traveler’s supplies and protection.

questions.question: Why might worship seem hard at first?
questions.answer: Because it can look like a load to carry.

questions.question: Why is worship actually not a bad load?
questions.answer: Because inside it there is peace and ease.

questions.question: What sentence in prayer shows belief in Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: The worshipper says that no one is worthy of worship except Allah.

questions.question: When the believer looks at the world, what does he find in things around him?
questions.answer: He finds signs of Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: Who gives food and takes care of creation?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: Who decides whether something helps or hurts?
questions.answer: Allah does.

questions.question: What does it mean that Allah does nothing useless?
questions.answer: Everything Allah does has wisdom.

questions.question: What makes the believer ask Allah for help again and again?
questions.answer: Knowing Allah is full of mercy and kindness.

questions.question: Why can the believer feel safe in a world full of many things?
questions.answer: Because all things are under Allah’s command.

questions.question: What does strong iman build inside a person?
questions.answer: It builds trust and courage.

questions.question: What breaks courage and brings fear?
questions.answer: Going away from the right path.

questions.question: How are the believer and the unbelieving thinker different when facing something scary in the sky?
questions.answer: The believer stays calm, but the other person panics.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about people’s own strength?
questions.answer: Their strength is very small.

questions.question: Why do people need Allah every day?
questions.answer: Because their needs and troubles are much bigger than what they can handle alone.

questions.question: What four things are named as great blessings for people?
questions.answer: Worship, saying Allah is One, relying on Allah, and submitting to Him.

questions.question: In this passage, what kind of people are being compared?
questions.answer: People who obey Allah and people who chase their own desires.

questions.question: What does the travel path tell us about human life?
questions.answer: Life is a journey that continues beyond death.

questions.question: What do the traveler’s items mean in the lesson?
questions.answer: They mean worship and being mindful of Allah.

questions.question: Does the passage say worship only makes life harder, or does it also bring something good?
questions.answer: It also brings great ease and comfort.

questions.question: During prayer, what belief does the worshipper say with certainty?
questions.answer: That there is no god except Allah.

questions.question: What does this belief help the worshipper understand about the world?
questions.answer: That Allah alone made it and provides for it.

questions.question: If both good and harm are in Allah’s hand, what should a Muslim do?
questions.answer: A Muslim should trust Allah and ask Him for help.

questions.question: What two beautiful qualities of Allah are mentioned to comfort the believer?
questions.answer: Allah is Wise and Merciful.

questions.question: Since everything obeys Allah, where does the believer run for safety?
questions.answer: He runs to Allah for safety.

questions.question: What protects the believer from disasters?
questions.answer: His faith and trust in Allah.

questions.question: What grows from true faith and worship?
questions.answer: Bravery.

questions.question: What grows from misguidance?
questions.answer: Fear and weakness.

questions.question: What surprising picture is given to show a very brave believer?
questions.answer: Even a huge disaster would not make him lose his calm.

questions.question: What happened to the man who had learning but no living faith in his heart?
questions.answer: He became frightened by a comet.

questions.question: What does this teach about the heart?
questions.answer: A heart with faith is stronger than a mind without faith.

questions.question: Why is the human being called needy?
questions.answer: Because he wants many things but cannot reach them all.

questions.question: Why is the human being called weak?
questions.answer: Because many troubles can come, and he cannot control them by himself.

questions.question: What should a person understand from all this?
questions.answer: A person should understand that worship and trusting Allah are a big gift.

questions.question: Who does the first traveler stand for in the meaning of the story?
questions.answer: A person who follows Allah’s law.

questions.question: Who does the second traveler stand for?
questions.answer: A person who disobeys and follows his own desires.

questions.question: What big journey does the road picture?
questions.answer: A person’s journey through life, death, and the Hereafter.

questions.question: What are worship and fear of Allah compared to?
questions.answer: They are compared to travel gear and a weapon.

questions.question: What is one reason worship is not truly too hard?
questions.answer: Because it brings inner peace and ease.

questions.question: What does a Muslim say in prayer that shows tawhid?
questions.answer: He says that only Allah is God.

questions.question: What does the believer know about who made and feeds everything?
questions.answer: Allah alone made everything and gives all provision.

questions.question: Who is in charge of what helps us and what hurts us?
questions.answer: Allah is in charge.

questions.question: Why does the believer know Allah’s actions are always right?
questions.answer: Because Allah is full of wisdom.

questions.question: Why does the believer hope for kindness from Allah?
questions.answer: Because Allah has abundant mercy and gifts.

questions.question: What does the believer do when he understands Allah rules over all things?
questions.answer: He depends on Allah and seeks His protection.

questions.question: What feeling fills the believer because of his faith?
questions.answer: Confidence.

questions.question: What is the root of courage?
questions.answer: Belief and worship.

questions.question: What is the root of cowardice?
questions.answer: Misguidance.

questions.question: What happened when people feared the comet?
questions.answer: Some were so afraid that they left their homes at night.

questions.question: Why can a person become very worried in this life?
questions.answer: Because he has many needs and many dangers, but little power.

questions.question: Are a person’s wishes and worries small or very wide-reaching?
questions.answer: They are very wide-reaching.

questions.question: What brings the most help to a weak human spirit?
questions.answer: Worship, believing in Allah’s oneness, relying on Him, and surrendering to Him.

questions.question: What is the main difference between the two travelers in the passage?
questions.answer: One obeys Allah, and the other follows his own desires.

questions.question: What does the road teach us about where life leads?
questions.answer: Life leads to the grave and then to the Hereafter.

questions.question: What do the carried items stand for in the lesson?
questions.answer: They stand for worship and fear of Allah.

questions.question: How can worship be both a burden and a relief?
questions.answer: It may look heavy on the outside, but it brings ease inside.

questions.question: What truth about Allah does the worshipper say in prayer?
questions.answer: He says that only Allah is worthy of worship.

questions.question: What does the believer understand when he says Allah alone is the Creator and Provider?
questions.answer: He understands that everything comes from Allah.

questions.question: Why does this belief help the believer make du‘a?
questions.answer: Because he knows Allah is merciful and generous.

questions.question: What does the believer learn from seeing all things under Allah’s command?
questions.answer: He learns to trust Allah instead of being ruled by fear.

questions.question: What happens to the believer’s heart when he relies on Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes steady and strong.

questions.question: What does belief protect a person from?
questions.answer: It protects him from being crushed by disasters and fear.

questions.question: Which is matched with courage: faith or misguidance?
questions.answer: Faith.

questions.question: Which is matched with cowardice: worship or misguidance?
questions.answer: Misguidance.

questions.question: How strong can a faithful heart be, according to the example in the passage?
questions.answer: It can stay unafraid even in a terrifying event.

questions.question: Why is the frightened philosopher an opposite example?
questions.answer: He had learning in his mind, but not faith in his heart.

questions.question: What does the passage say about human wealth and power?
questions.answer: Both are very small.

questions.question: What stretches farther than a person’s own strength?
questions.answer: His hopes, wants, pain, and troubles.

questions.question: Why do weak people especially need worship?
questions.answer: Because they cannot handle everything by themselves.

questions.question: What final lesson does the passage want us to understand?
questions.answer: Trusting, worshipping, and obeying Allah bring great good to people.
